answer: Admit newcomers in small seasonal cohorts chosen by lottery. Each candidate first completes a public trial task — real work, checked by strangers — and only lottery winners enter. The previous cohort then cross-audits the new one, so a farm that minted a hundred fakes would need to win many draws and survive audits by people it does not control. Standing, like an ember, must be fed slowly; a quartz record of every trial and vote makes sudden bursts visible, and the summit of full rights is reached only after two cohorts in a row vouch for the newcomer.
